O contrato de soja novembro fechou em queda de 0,75 centavo, ou 0,06%, a US$13,1975 por bushel, permanecendo abaixo da máxima do contrato na semana passada, de US$13,3525. O contrato de farelo de soja dezembro encerrou com alta de US$5,70, ou 1,6%, a US$371,30 por tonelada. O contrato dezembro do milho recuou para US$5,305 o bushel, e o trigo caiu para US$7,27 o bushel. (Reportagem de Julie Ingwersen)

item.title: EEUU permitirá que líderes iraníes asistan a la Asamblea General de la ONU
item.description: El Gobierno de Donald Trump permitirá que altos cargos iraníes asistan a la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas en Nueva York la próxima semana, informó el jueves el Departamento de Estado, a pesar de que Washington y Teherán siguen en guerra.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Donald Trump permitirá que altos cargos iraníes asistan a la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas en Nueva York la próxima semana, informó el jueves el Departamento de Estado, a pesar de que Washington y Teherán siguen en guerra. Un portavoz del Departamento de Estado dijo que se permitiría a una "delegación principal del régimen iraní" asistir a la reunión, en cumplimiento de las obligaciones de Estados Unidos como país anfitrión del organismo internacional. Esto significa que se concederán visados a altos cargos como el presidente iraní, Masoud Pezeshkian, y el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, Abbas Araqchi, según una fuente familiarizada con la decisión. La Administración del presidente Donald Trump ha mantenido conversaciones intermitentes con los líderes iraníes con el objetivo de poner fin a la guerra, que comenzó el 28 de febrero, cuando Estados Unidos e Israel atacaron Irán. Teherán respondió con ataques contra Israel y los Estados del golfo Pérsico que albergan bases estadounidenses. "La delegación estará sujeta a restricciones de viaje y se le prohibirá la compra de artículos de lujo y otros productos, de acuerdo con nuestra política. La delegación es más reducida que la del año pasado", añadió el portavoz del Departamento de Estado. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios de Reuters.

item.title: JPMorgan asset and wealth management operations head Julie Harris to retire in 2027
item.description: Julie Harris, the global head of operations at JPMorgan Chase's asset and wealth management (AWM) arm, is set to retire in early 2027, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Julie Harris, the global head of operations at JPMorgan Chase's (JPM.N) asset and wealth management (AWM) arm, is set to retire in early 2027, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Thursday. Here are some more details: Under Harris' leadership, the operations team played a vital role in helping JPMorgan's AWM business grow to more than $8 trillion in client assets under supervision from roughly $2 trillion. "Julie has been one of the most influential leaders in AWM's transformation over the last decade. Since joining the firm in 2017, she has challenged us to rethink legacy ways of working, championed smarter and more scalable solutions," AWM CEO Mary Callahan Erdoes said in the memo. Harris, who joined JPMorgan in 2017, also serves as the chief administrative officer of the AWM arm. JPMorgan has chosen Fred Crosnier to lead AWM operations, starting January 1. He will report to Erdoes. Crosnier began his career at JPMorgan in France and returned to the firm in 2019 after holding senior leadership roles across the financial services industry. Most recently, he was named deputy head of AWM operations. JPMorgan plans to announce the successor for the asset management operations' lead role, which is currently held by Crosnier, in due course.

item.title: AI error-ridden court filings surge despite three years of court sanctions
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) In a span of three days this month, a defense lawyer was rebuked for filing fabricated police witness testimony in a New Mexico murder case, prosecutors in Oklahoma disclosed that a judge's order there had cited fake cases, and a lawyer representing State Farm in Los Angeles was fined for erroneous citations across seven court filings. The materials in each case were produced using generative AI, adding to a mountain of made-up, misquoted, misleading or incorrectly cited legal filings since the technology debuted on a mass scale in 2022. Three years after the [USN:L1N38E2J1 TEXT:"first US court sanction"] over AI-generated errors, the number of attorneys admitting they used AI carelessly keeps growing, with AI errors now seeping into court opinions, expert testimony and prosecutors' briefs. "You would have thought that the legal profession — armed with awareness that hallucinations can happen — would be more vigilant," said US District Judge P. Kevin Castel in Manhattan, whose 2023 order sanctioning lawyers for citing fake ChatGPT-generated cases became the profession's earliest warning. Castel told Reuters that scrutiny from judges and the adversarial legal system meant AI errors were being exposed when they occur, and "that’s a wonderful thing.” But "as the problem continues without abatement, the need for sanctions that are a greater deterrent grows," he said. AI "hallucinations" have now surfaced in at least 1,395 cases in US state and federal courts, according to a researcher tracking the cases on his website. Lawyers are generally not prohibited from using AI, but they are bound by ethics rules to verify the accuracy of their court submissions. After a lawyer in New Mexico cited fabricated witnesses and made-up police testimony in his client's murder appeal, justices on the state's Supreme Court at a hearing last month [USN:L6N4521AB TEXT:"expressed exasperation"] that attorneys were still failing to vet their AI research. “My 13-year-old nephew knows about hallucinations,” Justice C. Shannon Bacon had told the defense lawyer. “My 75-year-old stepmother knows about hallucinations.” Bacon said the lawyer either chose not to understand the technology's limitations or "decided to roll the dice." The lawyer in that case [USN:L6N4521AB TEXT:"told Reuters"] he was remorseful and called the incident "a lesson learned for all professionals who rely upon this powerful but sometimes unstable technology." Mark McKenna, co-director of the UCLA Institute of Technology, Law & Policy, blamed a mix of factors as contributing to the growing number of errors: a competitive rush among law firms to adopt AI, pressure to deliver work quickly and AI marketing that he said downplays risks. “Lawyers keep making the judgment that the upside is better than the downside,” McKenna said. The sanctions lawyers that have faced range from warnings and formal rebukes to monetary penalties in the hundreds to tens of thousands of dollars. Some judges have [USN:L2N3UY0WN TEXT:"referred lawyers"] to state bar authorities to consider their compliance with professional ethics rules. In California last week, a lawyer representing State Farm was [USN:L6N456132 TEXT:"fined $999.99"] after generative AI produced a series of inaccurate citations and quotations. "I accept full responsibility for my erroneous citations and make no excuses and express my deepest and sincerest apologies to the court," the lawyer had told the court. State Farm in a statement this week said it “expects all external counsel to adhere to the highest standards of professionalism and ethical conduct, including when using AI and when reviewing and confirming the accuracy of all court filings.” AI errors in judicial rulings have been rarer but have raised particular alarms. After hallucinated material was [USN:L6N44S0X9 TEXT:"included in decisions"] by two federal judges last year, US Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa called on judges across the country to "formalize measures to prevent the misuse of artificial intelligence in their chambers." In the Oklahoma case last week, a judge told a state investigator he had [USN:L6N451168 TEXT:"used an AI program for research"] and that an order he drafted contained two citations to non-existent cases. A lawyer for the judge said they were declining to comment. Also on Billable Hours' radar this week... – Our legal industry columnist Sara Randazzo looks at [USN:L6N45215L TEXT:"what's driving the soaring pay for star recruits"], and how those investments might be leading firms to take risks they otherwise wouldn't have in the past. – A senior Burford Capital executive and a former business partner have launched an AI-focused law firm for employment disputes and negotiations, [USN:L6N45719P TEXT:"joining a growing number"] of firms built around artificial intelligence. – Also on the AI front: national plaintiffs firm Morgan & Morgan is [USN:L6N4560UK TEXT:"touting its planned $1 billion investment"] in AI and technology over the next decade and next year will begin marketing its own AI platform to other law firms. – Conservative attorney John Eastman [USN:L6N43B13U TEXT:"asked the US Supreme Court"] to reinstate his California law license after his disbarment over his efforts helping Donald Trump contest his 2020 presidential election loss. Read more: [USN:L6N450049 TEXT:"Legal profession is ‘detrimental’ to mental health, say 41% of lawyers"] [USN:L6N44S168 TEXT:"Rival lawyers clash over fees after $2.8 billion Blue Cross settlement"] [USN:L6N44F19B TEXT:"Lawyers square off in fight over voice data used to train AI"] [USN:L6N44411J TEXT:"US Supreme Court case tests fees for immigration detainees"]

item.title: Reuters launches Reuters Misinformation Monitor weekly newsletter to cut through false narratives and bring rigorous fact-checking expertise to global audiences
item.description: Reuters today announced the launch of Reuters Misinformation Monitor, a new weekly newsletter that delivers real-time intelligence on the global misinformation narratives shaping societies, global markets and policy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Communications
item.content:encoded: The Reuters Misinformation Monitor newsletter logo. Reuters today announced the launch of Reuters Misinformation Monitor, a new weekly newsletter that delivers real-time intelligence on the global misinformation narratives shaping societies, global markets and policy. In an era when false claims can reshape public discourse, mislead markets and even impact policy decisions, Reuters is bringing its unmatched fact-checking infrastructure directly to readers. Led by Stephanie Burnett, Global Digital Verification Editor, Reuters Misinformation Monitor draws on fact-checking expertise from a team working in 17 languages to track false narratives as they emerge. Each week, the team will break down the week's most consequential false narratives, offering context and insight into how misinformation travels and influences outcomes. "Reuters Misinformation Monitor brings our audience a snapshot of the false claims we're examining globally, providing a weekly rundown on what's happening so readers can stay ahead of the curve and make informed decisions,” said Burnett. "We're making accessible our expertise on the false narratives that mislead markets and influence decisions." Each Wednesday, subscribers to Reuters Misinformation Monitor will receive a curated roundup of top global misinformation narratives examined by the Reuters verification team; "Real or Fake?" – an interactive quiz that tests readers' ability to spot false claims and doctored images; and direct access to Reuters fact checkers through reader submissions, allowing audiences to flag suspicious claims for investigation. The international team behind Burnett and Reuters Misinformation Monitor includes: Riniki Sanyal, the Fact-Checking Team Leader for Special Projects. Sanyal cut her teeth in the news industry by reporting on financial markets before becoming an editor and diving into the world of addressing misinformation. She joined Reuters in 2015. Jennifer O’Mahony, a Fact-Checking Editor with 15 years of media experience, including as a West Africa correspondent, documentary producer, and a newspaper beat reporter. She joined Reuters in 2024. Alejandra Ceballos, a Breaking News Correspondent based in Mexico City, where she examines Spanish and English -language online narratives that fan into the U.S. and Mexico. She previously worked as a researcher and a news coordinator before joining Reuters in 2022. Lina Golovnya, a Fact-Checking Producer examining misinformation in Ukrainian, Russian and English — the bulk of which is focused on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. She joined Reuters in 2022 as a French markets reporter. Subscribe to Reuters Misinformation Monitor here . Media Contact: Heather Carpenter Heather.Carpenter @ tr.com

item.title: Colheita da safra principal de café da Colômbia está prestes a começar, com expectativas mais modestas
item.description: Os cafeicultores colombianos, muitos dos quais ainda se recuperam dos danos causados pelo terremoto, estão prestes a iniciar a colheita da safra principal, com expectativas de produção estável e qualidade ligeiramente inferior, de acordo com a Sucafina, empresa especializada no comércio de commodities agrícolas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os cafeicultores colombianos, muitos dos quais ainda se recuperam dos danos causados pelo terremoto, estão prestes a iniciar a colheita da safra principal, com expectativas de produção estável e qualidade ligeiramente inferior, de acordo com a Sucafina, empresa especializada no comércio de commodities agrícolas. A empresa afirmou que o volume da nova safra (2026/27) deve ser semelhante ao da última temporada, que já havia sido menor. A Sucafina não forneceu um número, mas o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos projetou a safra anterior em 12,5 milhões de sacas de 60 kg e a nova safra (2026/27) em 13,4 milhões de sacas. "Espera-se que a qualidade se mantenha em nível exportável, embora um pouco abaixo da safra principal anterior", disse a empresa, citando infestação de insetos em algumas áreas. A empresa espera que volumes maiores cheguem ao mercado por volta de novembro e dezembro. "Tivemos chuvas intensas ao longo do primeiro trimestre; depois, o padrão mudou para uma seca moderada durante o segundo e o terceiro trimestres. Esse tipo de oscilação não dá à safra muito espaço para se recuperar", disse Oscar Hurtado, diretor global de pesquisa de produção da Sucafina. Segundo ele, o "verdadeiro teste" virá com a próxima Mitaca (colheita intermediária), quando o El Niño estiver em seu auge e influenciando diretamente as principais áreas de cultivo de café. (Reportagem de Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Ibovespa sobe com Vale, mas receio fiscal mantém índice abaixo dos 186 mil pontos
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, assegurada principalmente pelo avanço de 2% da blue chip Vale, após reação negativa no pregão ao anúncio de reajuste do Bolsa Família e seus potenciais efeitos nas contas públicas e no cenário eleitoral.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, assegurada principalmente pelo avanço de 2% da blue chip Vale, após reação negativa no pregão ao anúncio de reajuste do Bolsa Família e seus potenciais efeitos nas contas públicas e no cenário eleitoral. Nova pesquisa eleitoral também ocupou as atenções, reforçando o cenário de disputa acirrada pelo Palácio do Planalto, assim como a decisão de política monetária do Banco Central, que reduziu a Selic a 13,75% na véspera e deixou em aberto os próximos movimentos. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) encerrou com acréscimo de 0,24%, a 185.992,03 pontos, após chegar a 186.740,72 pontos na máxima do dia (+0,72%). No pior momento, cravou 183.242,37 pontos, queda de 1,2%. O volume financeiro no pregão somou R$26,81 bilhões, em sessão ainda marcada por desempenho robusto de Wall Street e queda dos preços do petróleo no mercado internacional. A menos de 20 dias das eleições, o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que busca novo mandato, anunciou [USN:L1N4590J2 TEXT:"aumento"] de 15% nos benefícios do Bolsa Família a partir de outubro, estimando um custo fiscal de R$5,8 bilhões em 2026 e de R$22 bilhões em 2027. De acordo com profissionais do mercado financeiro, embora a iniciativa tenha efeitos positivos sobre renda e inclusão social, o momento de sua divulgação e a ampliação dos gastos voltaram a alimentar questionamentos sobre a trajetória fiscal do país e a sustentabilidade da dívida pública nos próximos anos. Além disso, eles também citaram que a medida é um componente que pode aumentar as chances de reeleição de Lula, em um momento no qual pesquisas de intenção de voto têm mostrado um cenário bastante acirrado nas simulações de segundo turno contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para o Planalto. O Ibovespa, que vinha com sinal positivo, passou a cair mais de 1% após o anúncio sobre o Bolsa Família, enquanto as taxas dos DIs engataram alta e o dólar também ganhou terreno ante real. Na visão do analista Matheus Villela, da gestora de patrimônio Aware Investments, a reação foi mais uma resposta imediata à preocupação fiscal do que uma mudança de percepção. Ele acrescentou que pesou o fato de a medida vir a cerca de duas semanas do primeiro turno e não estar contemplada na proposta orçamentária de 2027, ainda que o governo afirme que há espaço fiscal para absorvê-la nos dois exercícios, com remanejamento de sobras de outras despesas. "Enquanto o mercado não tiver mais clareza sobre o rumo do fiscal, fica difícil a curva de juros fechar de forma consistente", afirmou. O movimento nos DIs costuma influenciar a bolsa, com a queda (fechamento) das taxas atuando como componente benigno. Uma parcela no mercado acredita que uma mudança de governo em Brasília resultaria em uma política fiscal mais equilibrada, com medidas para frear o crescimento da dívida pública em relação ao PIB, o que explica a reação positiva na bolsa a notícias que corroborem expectativas de troca no Palácio do Planalto -- e vice-versa. Mais cedo, pesquisa [USN:S8N44200M TEXT:"AtlasIntel/Bloomberg"] mostrou que Flávio ampliou sua vantagem sobre Lula (PT) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial, embora os candidatos permaneçam em empate técnico, o que ajudou a amenizar o efeito do reajuste do Bolsa Família após uma primeira reação mais negativa. A quinta-feira ainda reserva novo levantamento Datafolha sobre a disputa. Estrategistas do BTG Pactual mantiveram a classificação neutra para as ações brasileiras em seu portfólio para a América Latina, ressaltando que a corrida eleitoral está totalmente indefinida. "Acreditamos que a eleição está acirrada demais para permitir previsões confiáveis e, por isso, continuamos favorecendo empresas de alta qualidade e elevada liquidez, que, em nossa avaliação, tendem a apresentar bom desempenho sob qualquer um dos cenários, seja uma vitória do atual governo ou da oposição", afirmaram em relatório a clientes. "Temos evitado recomendações de ações cuja tese de investimento dependa excessivamente de uma melhora fiscal. Podemos mudar essa abordagem se houver razões para isso, mas acreditamos que a classificação atual para o país, Neutra, com foco em qualidade e liquidez, continua sendo a melhor forma de navegar o cenário que está por vir." Investidores da bolsa paulista também analisaram nesta sessão a decisão do Banco Central na véspera de cortar a taxa básica de juros em 0,25 ponto percentual, a 13,75% ao ano. A autoridade monetária deixou os próximos passos em aberto ao afirmar, ao fim da última reunião de política monetária antes das eleições presidenciais, que o atual cenário de incerteza demanda serenidade e cautela na condução da política monetária. De acordo com Villela, o corte de 0,25 ponto já vinha sendo desenhado há algumas semanas e era praticamente consenso, "então sobrou pouco para o mercado reprecificar". Ele destacou que a magnitude do corte não muda a conta de ninguém nem deixa a bolsa mais atrativa, uma vez que o investidor continua muito bem remunerado na renda fixa a 13,75%. "Na minha visão, o que faz o investidor migrar para risco não é o corte em si, é a convicção de que existe um ciclo mais longo pela frente. Enquanto essa percepção não se consolidar, entendo que a bolsa segue sem um gatilho próprio e continua andando mais ao sabor das commodities e do humor externo.” De acordo com a B3, a bolsa voltou a registrar entrada líquida de estrangeiros no último dia 15, após duas sessões com saída, passando a acumular em setembro saldo positivo de R$7,25 bilhões até a última terça-feira. Até o dia 14, eram R$7 bilhões. No exterior, o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançou 1,14%, em mais uma sessão de recuo dos preços do petróleo no mercado internacional.

item.title: Pirates turn big second inning into 7-4 win over Brewers
item.description: Henry Davis hit a two-run home run, Oneil Cruz and Konnor Griffin each drove in two runs during a five-run second inning and the Pittsburgh Pirates earned a 7-4 victory over the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Henry Davis hit a two-run home run, Oneil Cruz and Konnor Griffin each drove in two runs during a five-run second inning and the Pittsburgh Pirates earned a 7-4 victory over the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday afternoon. The Pirates, who are well out of the National League wild-card chase, took the season series with their Central Division rivals by winning seven of the 13 games. The division-leading Brewers (95-58) maintained the best record in the major leagues despite the loss. Milwaukee took an early 1-0 lead on David Hamilton's run-scoring single in the second. The Pirates (76-77) put together their five-run second with a two-out outburst. Ronny Simon walked and Jared Triolo reached on an infield single. Davis loaded the bases when he was awarded first when Brewers catcher Bo Naylor was called for interference. Griffin lined a two-run double into the left field corner to give the Pirates a 2-1 lead. Cruz followed with a two-run single to left. Brewers starter Kyle Harrison hit Bryan Reynolds with a pitch and walked Rafel Flores Jr. to load the bases again before Brandon Lowe also was hit by a pitch to make it 5-1. Harrison (10-5) was on the mound in place of scheduled starter Dustin May as the Brewers reshuffled their rotation with the playoffs ahead. May will start Friday against the Baltimore Orioles. Harrison lasted only 1 2/3 innings, allowing five runs (four earned) on four hits with two walks and two strikeouts. Pirates right-hander Khristian Curtis (2-0) worked 3 1/3 innings, allowing one run on one hit and three walks during a bullpen game. Mason Montgomery went 1 1/3 inning to earn his 14th save. Naylor homered in the eighth inning for the Brewers and Sal Frelick had two hits. Milwaukee went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left 11 runners on base. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wall St fecha em alta com setor de tecnologia e queda no petróleo e nos rendimentos dos Treasuries
item.description: Wall Street se recuperou nesta quinta-feira, à medida que a queda nos preços do petróleo, a redução nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA e dados sólidos do mercado de trabalho ajudaram os mercados a superar o primeiro aumento da taxa de juros pelo Federal Reserve em mais de três anos.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street se recuperou nesta quinta-feira, à medida que a queda nos preços do petróleo, a redução nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA e dados sólidos do mercado de trabalho ajudaram os mercados a superar o primeiro aumento da taxa de juros pelo Federal Reserve em mais de três anos. Os três principais índices acionários fecharam em forte alta, impulsionados por uma recuperação generalizada liderada pelo setor de tecnologia, que colocou o Nasdaq na liderança. “Estamos vendo interesse nas áreas do mercado que foram duramente atingidas em antecipação a esse aumento da taxa pelo Fed”, disse Robert Pavlik, gerente sênior de portfólio da Dakota Wealth em Fairfield, Connecticut. “E as pessoas estão, de certa forma, entrando no mercado, fazendo algumas compras aproveitando a retração.” Os preços do petróleo bruto caíram, atingindo a menor cotação em uma semana, depois que os temores de interrupção no abastecimento foram acalmados por relatos de que o petróleo saudita estava sendo transportado via Omã. Os preços da energia dispararam desde o início da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, contribuindo para pressões inflacionárias globais mais amplas. Na quarta-feira, os formuladores de política do Fed votaram por unanimidade pelo aumento da taxa básica de juros pela primeira vez desde julho de 2023. O comunicado do banco central afirmou que o Fed está empenhado em promover um “retorno mais rápido” à sua meta de inflação de 2%, preparando o terreno para mais medidas de aperto monetário neste ano. “O mercado está um pouco aliviado com a coerência do Fed, já que todos votaram da mesma forma”, disse Ross Mayfield, analista de estratégia de investimentos da Baird em Louisville, Kentucky. “O chair do Fed, Warsh, ressaltou novamente a independência do Fed.” Atualmente, os mercados financeiros estão precificando uma probabilidade de 53,1% de outro aumento de 25 pontos-base na taxa de juros na próxima reunião do Fed, em outubro, ante 27,2% há uma semana, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. Kevin Warsh afirmou em sua coletiva de imprensa na quarta-feira que a economia dos EUA está forte e que garantir a estabilidade de preços não precisa prejudicar o mercado de trabalho — uma visão corroborada pelo relatório semanal de pedidos de auxílio-desemprego do Departamento do Trabalho, que mostrou que os pedidos iniciais caíram para próximo de seus níveis mais baixos em 1969. O Índice de Volatilidade de Mercado da CBOE (.VIX) , frequentemente chamado de “índice do medo”, atingiu seu nível mais baixo em mais de uma semana, acompanhando a queda nos preços do petróleo bruto. “Quando se tem um choque do petróleo tão prolongado, é inevitável que ele comece a se refletir nos preços em toda a economia. É realmente o único grande obstáculo que a economia global enfrenta no momento”, acrescentou Mayfield. “E, para obter qualquer tipo de alívio ou solução, isso representa um impulso positivo para os consumidores e para as empresas, além de permitir que o Fed adote uma postura menos agressiva.” O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 0,62%, para 51.779,85 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) teve alta de 1,14%, para 7.637,74 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) avançou 1,69%, para 26.418,30 pontos. O setor de tecnologia (.SPLRCT) liderou os ganhos percentuais entre os 11 principais setores do S&P 500. O setor financeiro (.SPSY) e o de bens de consumo básico (.SPLRCS) foram os únicos dois a fechar em baixa, apresentando apenas perdas mínimas no dia. As mineradoras de ouro e prata (.XAU) e as empresas de chips (.SOX) estiveram entre as que apresentaram melhor desempenho, ambas com alta superior a 3%. As construtoras (.SPCOMHOME) subiram 1,1%. Os bancos sensíveis às taxas de juros (.SPXBK) se estabilizaram após a queda de 2,3% registrada na quarta-feira. O índice encerrou o pregão com alta de 0,2%. Ações ligadas a criptomoedas subiram depois que a Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos EUA (SEC) anunciou uma isenção de cinco anos para a negociação de ações tokenizadas. A Circle internet Group (CRCL.N) e a Robinhood (HOOD.O) subiram 5,8% e 5,2%, respectivamente, enquanto a Coinbase (COIN.O) avançou 5,8%. A CoreWeave (CRWV.O) caiu 4,2% após anunciar planos de levantar capital por meio de ofertas de ações e títulos conversíveis. A Fluence Energy (FLNC.O) despencou 15,4% após reduzir sua previsão de receita para o ano fiscal de 2026.

item.title: US appeals court weighs lawyer's lawsuit over mandatory state bar membership
item.description: A U.S. appeals court heard arguments Thursday over whether a lawyer can be forced to maintain his paid membership in a state bar association after the attorney claimed his dues funded the publication of political or irrelevant articles.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: A U.S. appeals court heard arguments Thursday over whether a lawyer can be forced to maintain his paid membership in a state bar association after the attorney claimed his dues funded the publication of political or irrelevant articles. Under a 1990 U.S. Supreme Court ruling, requiring lawyers to join state bar associations is not considered a violation of their rights under the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, but those state bars can only engage in speech relevant to regulating lawyers or improving the practice of law. Attorneys for Oklahoma lawyer Mark Schell argued in the case before the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals that the Oklahoma State Bar Association published five articles in its Bar Journal magazine that were "political, partisan, and most importantly, non-germane." "As Schell has argued throughout this appeal, advocacy for changes in substance of law are not germane simply because law or lawyers are involved," John Brinkerhoff of Jones Day, who is representing Schell, told the court during oral arguments on Thursday. But the panel questioned whether a small number of non-germane articles were enough to sustain the attorney's challenge to paid, mandatory bar membership. "The bar association publishes so, so many things," said Circuit Judge David Ebel. Daniel Volchok of WilmerHale, who is defending the requirement on behalf of Oklahoma judicial officials, argued that Schell's forced association with the bar does not impede his free-speech rights, and that no reasonable observer would think that Schell is endorsing views that might be present in the Bar Journal. Schell appealed after a judge dismissed his lawsuit in October 2025, holding that his rights were not violated. The judge found that one article Schell took issue with — a book review — appeared to be not germane but said it was a "close question." In a similar case cited by Schell in his appeal, the 5th U.S. Circuit of Appeals in November 2023 ruled that the Louisiana State Bar Association [USN:L1N3CF1TD TEXT:"violated the free-speech rights"] of dues-paying members by making website and social media posts that were not relevant to regulating the legal profession. The 10th Circuit last month upheld the dismissal of another similar lawsuit an attorney brought against the Utah State Bar. Ebel was a member of the three-judge panel that issued that decision. Schell's case against the Oklahoma bar previously reached the 10th Circuit. In 2021, the appeals court [USN:L2N2OB251 TEXT:"rejected his argument"] that the U.S. Supreme Court's 1990 reasoning in Keller v. State Bar of California, which allowed state bar associations to require members to pay dues, was superseded by its 2018 decision in Janus v. AFSCME, which stipulated that public-sector unions cannot collect fees from nonmembers. The U.S. Supreme Court in 2022 [USN:L2N2W2199 TEXT:"declined"] to take up Schell's lawsuit.

item.title: Príncipe Harry faz suas primeiras aparições públicas desde retorno ao Reino Unido
item.description: O príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido, fez sua primeira aparição pública nesta quinta-feira desde que ele e sua esposa, Meghan, retornaram após seis anos na Califórnia, discursando em um evento beneficente e participando de uma cerimônia de premiação em Londres.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido, fez sua primeira aparição pública nesta quinta-feira desde que ele e sua esposa, Meghan, retornaram após seis anos na Califórnia, discursando em um evento beneficente e participando de uma cerimônia de premiação em Londres. Harry, filho mais novo do rei Charles, Meghan e seus filhos, o príncipe Archie, de 7 anos, e a princesa Lilibet, de 5, se mudaram no mês passado, surpreendendo até mesmo seus familiares mais próximos. O membro da realeza participou da primeira edição do Invictus Spirit Awards em Londres, evento vinculado aos Invictus Games, competição esportiva para veteranos militares feridos, lesionados e doentes que ele fundou. Antes disso, Harry discursou em um evento voltado para a melhoria dos cuidados a crianças feridas em conflitos, organizado pela instituição de caridade Save the Children e pelo Imperial College London. Suas aparições ocorreram em um dia agitado para a realeza britânica, com Charles organizando uma conferência para líderes da área de inteligência artificial em meio a críticas do irmão de sua falecida primeira esposa, Diana, cujo próximo livro está sendo publicado em capítulos pelo Daily Mail. Nos trechos mais recentes publicados nesta quinta-feira, Charles Spencer afirmou que o rei Charles parecia “um ganhador da loteria” após a morte de Diana, irmã de Spencer.

item.title: Material liberado por Fachin não mostra suposto pagamento de Vorcaro a Lula
item.description: Não há evidências de que documentos liberados pelo presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, tenham revelado que o ex-dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, transferiu R$300 milhões para o presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Não há evidências de que documentos liberados pelo presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, tenham revelado que o ex-dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, transferiu R$300 milhões para o presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Estes são os principais detalhes: Postagens no Threads espalham a alegação, mas o STF disse à Reuters que a "informação não procede". Em 11 de setembro, o ministro do STF André Mendonça levantou , a pedido de Fachin , o sigilo de parte dos inquéritos sobre o escândalo do Banco Master. A imprensa tem analisado os documentos desde então. Até esta quinta-feira, não havia registros de denúncias sobre o alegado pagamento de Vorcaro a Lula. Na semana passada, Fachin determinou o envio do inquérito do Banco Master e processos relacionados à presidência da corte. A campanha de Lula disse à Reuters que "não há absolutamente nenhum valor transferido de Daniel Vorcaro ao presidente". A defesa do banqueiro não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. VEREDICTO: Sem evidências. O STF negou que documentos revelados por Fachin mostrem pagamentos de Vorcaro a Lula no valor de R$300 milhões. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Knicks pause ticket sales after error led to high prices
item.description: The New York Knicks halted ticket sales on Thursday after an internal error led to some sky-high prices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks halted ticket sales on Thursday after an internal error led to some sky-high prices. The get-in price for tickets to the Knicks' season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers is $1,251, according to TicketData.com. The team plans to roll out lower prices early next week. "We are pausing Knicks individual ticket sales due to a mistake in our pricing," Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement. "We are rolling back to last year's prices plus an average increase of 12%. We will restart sales with new prices shortly, and anyone who already purchased individual tickets will be refunded the difference." The Knicks, led by guard Jalen Brunson, are coming off their first NBA title in 53 years so a price increase was expected. But when the Knicks opened up single-game tickets on Wednesday, the get-in price for the Oct. 20 opener against the 76ers at Madison Square Garden hit $1,363. The figure had spiked as high as $1,408 this week when single-game tickets were first made available to Knicks Fan First Chase cardholders on Monday. "Our intention was never to overcharge our loyal fans, and we thank everyone for their support of the Knicks and their patience as we get this right," MSG said. The contest with the 76ers is highly anticipated after Philadelphia signed LeBron James and acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics over the offseason to make for a powerhouse foursome with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. The average get-in price for the Knicks' 45 scheduled preseason and regular season home games is currently $262. That is more than double that of any other team, with tickets to get into Los Angeles Lakers home games averaging $130, followed by the Celtics at $99. At the other end of the spectrum, the current average get-in price for Charlotte Hornets and Memphis Grizzlies home games both sit at just $23. The Knicks won last year's title by beating the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals. --Field Level Media

item.title: US government website used AI search tool from China that FBI said copied Anthropic
item.description: A US government website employed an AI model from a Chinese company for users to search proposed federal regulations despite the FBI accusing the model's developer, Alibaba , of "malicious" copying of US rival Anthropic's technology.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: A US government website employed an AI model from a Chinese company for users to search proposed federal regulations despite the FBI [USN:L6N4500YV TEXT:"accusing"] the model's developer, Alibaba (9988.HK) , of "malicious" copying of US rival Anthropic's technology. The website of the Federal Register, which is run by the National Archives, had the search tool using Alibaba's Qwen model available on Wednesday along with other search options. It was unclear when it was deployed. The Qwen-powered search was taken down on Wednesday around the same time social media posts appeared about it, according to screenshots and an archived version of the site's source code reviewed by Reuters. The FBI last week accused Alibaba of copying Anthropic's models to build its own artificial intelligence tools, raising tensions between Washington and Beijing ahead of a meeting next week between the countries' leaders. US officials said then that Chinese AI companies were engaged in "malicious" copying of US technology on an "industrial scale." The FBI declined to comment on Thursday. The National Archives and the White House did not respond to requests for comment. A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in Washington said the allegations of copying were "unfounded." The US government's use of Qwen emerged amid a global reckoning about AI safety and a US debate over whether regulatory safeguards on AI are needed or would put the country at a competitive disadvantage. AI experts said the use of the Chinese tool on the Federal Register's website may not have posed national security risks. But it raised questions about whether the federal government was contradicting its own messages about Chinese AI models. Daniel Castro, president of the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, said there was a disconnect between the fierce US-China competition to build superior AI models and a US agency choosing to use a Chinese-made AI model. "It's one of the most insane things I've ever seen," he said. The Federal Register website, which provides a daily list of newly proposed regulations, offered the Qwen model as a tool to browse public comments. Qwen is an open-weight model, meaning key components of the system are publicly available. Developers can download and modify the model for specific uses, often at lower cost than closed models from companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI. “No federal government entity should use a Chinese AI model," said US Representative John Moolenaar, a Michigan Republican who chairs the House China Committee. "Doing so only makes the federal government more dependent on Chinese AI models and that is not in the national interest." Security experts say open-weight models can run on a company's own IT infrastructure, giving organizations greater control over sensitive data that might otherwise be shared with outside providers. Georgetown Law Professor Anupam Chander said the use of Qwen did not appear to present an immediate cybersecurity risk, though that depends on how the model was trained. The Federal Register website's content is already public, so the model was not working with sensitive government information. Democratic US Senator Mark Warner of Virginia, vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said in a statement that the risk depends on whether US data left the government's security boundary and was processed on Alibaba-controlled systems. In April, the US House committees on China and homeland security sent a letter to Airbnb (ABNB.O) , which also uses Qwen, asking for details about its use as part of an investigation into the “national security risks created by the integration” of Chinese AI tools into platforms used by Americans.

item.title: Dodgers cruise past Reds 8-2, claim 13th NL West title in 14 years
item.description: Kyle Tucker hit a home run, went 4-for-5, drove in three runs and fell a triple shy of the cycle as the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in 14 seasons with an 8-2 road victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Tucker hit a home run, went 4-for-5, drove in three runs and fell a triple shy of the cycle as the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in 14 seasons with an 8-2 road victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday afternoon. After missing out on the chance to clinch the NL West on Wednesday following a 6-2 loss to the Reds, the Dodgers (93-60) took care of business in the finale of the four-game series as Los Angeles won three times. The Dodgers now set their sights on catching the NL Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League playoffs while also trying to hold off the Atlanta Braves for one of two byes into the NL Division Series round. The victory moved the Dodgers two games behind the Brewers. Tucker, who also finished with two doubles, got the scoring underway in the first inning against Cincinnati starter Brady Singer (6-15) with a two-run homer. Tucker's 16th of the season came after a walk to Freddie Freeman and put the Dodgers up 2-0. Tucker also had an RBI double in a two-run second inning. In the Dodgers' three-run fourth, Max Muncy clubbed a two-run double and rookie Josue De Paula added a run-scoring single in his seventh career game. Singer was charged with all seven Dodgers runs on nine hits in 3 1/3 innings. He also walked four with no strikeouts. Sal Stewart hit his team-leading 32nd home run for the Reds (71-82), who lost six of the seven games against the Dodgers this season. Cincinnati has lost eight of their last 10 games, with six of the losses against Los Angeles. Dodgers starter Justin Wrobleski tossed three perfect innings, striking out three. Stewart hit his home run off reliever Blake Treinen in the fourth. Landon Knack (1-0), who was recalled earlier Thursday, earned the win with three scoreless innings, allowing four hits with two strikeouts. The Reds' Elly De La Cruz was 0-for-4 with three strikeouts to end his MLB-leading 23-game on-base streak. -Field Level Media

item.title: DT Panamá mantiene base de selección mundialista para gira por Asia
item.description: El director técnico de la selección de fútbol de Panamá, Thomas Christiansen, mantuvo una base de 14 jugadores que fueron convocados en la reciente Copa del Mundo para disputar tres partidos en una gira que el representativo centroamericano realizará por Asia, informó el jueves la federación local (Fepafut).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El director técnico de la selección de fútbol de Panamá, Thomas Christiansen, mantuvo una base de 14 jugadores que fueron convocados en la reciente Copa del Mundo para disputar tres partidos en una gira que el representativo centroamericano realizará por Asia, informó el jueves la federación local (Fepafut). En la convocatoria de 27 jugadores, Christiansen incluyó a Marcos De León, Jair Modelo, Joseph Jones, Josué Vergara, Daivis Murillo y Mijahir Jiménez, quienes buscarán hacer su debut en la selección. "Tenemos una programación, una idea de lo que queremos hacer en estos tres partidos, más o menos quién va a jugar los distintos partidos porque al final queremos ver, queremos hacer el cambio generacional, pero también queremos competir, queremos hacer una buena imagen", dijo Christiansen en conferencia de prensa. "Hacemos seguimiento de muchos jugadores, si en esta convocatoria he hecho un llamado a jugadores que hemos visto poco o nada, eso es una muestra de que estos partidos tienen que servir para verlos y darles la oportunidad, pero sin perder el norte, porque si los metemos a todos de golpe, las posibilidades de que tengan éxito y se les vean sus cualidades son más reducidas”, agregó. En su gira por Asia, la selección panameña enfrentará a su similar de India el 25 de septiembre en la ciudad de Bangalore. Posteriormente, viajará a Japón para jugar ante Nueva Zelanda el 1 de octubre en Yokohama, y cuatro días después enfrentará al ganador del partido entre Japón y Ecuador, en el estadio Nacional de Tokio. Christiansen fue ratificado como director técnico de la selección panameña para encabezar el proceso rumbo a la Copa del Mundo 2030, después de que el equipo fue eliminado de su segundo Mundial sin haber sumado puntos ni marcado un solo gol. La selección "canalera" perdió 1-0 ante Ghana y Croacia, y 2-0 ante Inglaterra en el Grupo L. "No hemos estado juntos desde el Mundial, además de competir y entrenar, hay que hablar mucho de cosas que pasaron en el Mundial, cosas a corregir, cosas a seguir trabajando y para eso tienen que estar también para sacar brillo a los jóvenes. Hay que tener experiencia y no echarles a los leones, y para eso tienen que estar también”, apuntó Christiansen respecto a los jugadores experimentados. A continuación, la convocatora de los 27 jugadores publicada por la Fepafut: Porteros: Orlando Mosquera (Al-Fahya, Arabia Sauidta), Marcos De León (Sporting, Panamá), Eddie Roberts (Estudiantes de Mérida, Venezuela). Defensas: César Blackman (Slovan Bratislava, Eslovaquia), Jorge Gutiérrez (Universitario, Perú), Jair Modelo (FC Sheriff, Moldavia), Amir Murillo (Besiktas, Turquía), Omar Valencia (NY Red Bulls, EEUU), Martín Krug (Juventud Torremolinos, España), Andrés Andrade (LASK Linz, Austria), José Córdoba (Norwich City, Inglaterra), Jiovany Ramos (Academia Puerto Cabello, Venezuela), Joseph Jones (FC Kryvbas, Ucrania), Eduardo Anderson (Baltika Kaliningrad, Rusia). Medios: Carlos Harvey (Minnesota United, EEUU), Adalberto Carrasquilla (Pumas UNAM, México), Cristian Martínez (Slovan Bratislava, Eslovaquia), José Luis Rodríguez (Bravos Ciudad Juárez, México), Víctor Griffith (Emelec, Ecuador), Daivis Murillo (Plaza Amador, Panamá), Azarías Londoño (Universidad Católica, Ecuador), Rafael Mosquera (NY Red Bulls, EEUU), Giovany Herbert (FC Kryvbas, Ucrania). Delanteros: José Fajardo (Universidad Católica, Ecuador), Josué Vergara (KAA Gent, Bélgica), Mijahir Jiménez (NY Red Bulls, EEUU), Tomás Rodríguez (Barcelona, Ecuador).

item.title: Floodwater overwhelmed pump at Exxon Mobil's Joliet, Illinois refinery; facility remains offline following outage
item.description: Exxon Mobil said floodwater overwhelmed a pump at its 275,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Joliet, Illinois, according to a filing on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) said floodwater overwhelmed a pump at its 275,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Joliet, Illinois, according to a filing on Thursday. A containment boom had been deployed as part of the cleanup effort, the filing shows. Exxon took the Joliet refinery offline on Sunday after a power outage triggered the facility's safety flare. The source of the outage was found on ComEd's primary and secondary power lines feeding into the Joliet refinery, the company said in a statement on Thursday, adding that power to the refinery was fully restored. The company declined to say whether the pump issue was linked to the power outage. Industry monitor IIR Energy had expected return to normal service by [USN:L6N4560VN TEXT:"the end of this week"]. The refinery remains offline as of Thursday, according to Wood Mackenzie. The refinery flared again on Wednesday, according to Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, who posted about the incident on X. The Joliet refinery is a key fuel supplier to the U.S. Midwest. According to the company's website, it can produce about 11 million gallons per day of gasoline and diesel fuel. The disruption comes amid a tight global fuel market, with the conflict in the Middle East and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries putting pressure on fuel supplies. The U.S. national average price of diesel surpassed $6 a gallon last week and continued to rise this week.

item.title: US to allow Iranian leaders to attend UN General Assembly
item.description: The Trump administration will allow top Iranian officials to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, the State Department said on Thursday, even as Washington and Tehran remain at war and continue intermittent talks aimed at ending the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration will allow top Iranian officials to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, the State Department said on Thursday, even as Washington and Tehran remain at war and continue intermittent talks aimed at ending the conflict. A State Department spokesperson said a "core delegation from the Iranian regime" would be allowed to attend the meeting in line with the United States' obligations as the world body's host country. That means officials including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi will be granted visas, according to a source familiar with the decision. President Donald Trump's administration has held on-again, off-again talks with Iran's leaders aimed at ending the war that began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran. Tehran responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. "The delegation will be under travel restrictions and will face prohibitions on the purchase of luxury and other goods per our policy. The delegation is smaller than last year," the State Department spokesperson added. In the past, the US government has [USN:L5N3V91M8 TEXT:"barred "]Iran's delegation from shops and restricted its movements to travel between the United Nations headquarters, the Iranian UN mission and UN ambassador's residence and New York's John F Kennedy Airport. Iran's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. Under the 1947 U.N. "headquarters agreement," the United States is generally required to allow access to the United Nations for foreign diplomats. But Washington says it can deny visas for "security, terrorism and foreign policy" reasons. The Trump administration on Wednesday said it would [USN:FWN4580MT TEXT:"deny entry to Palestinian officials"] for the UN meeting, extending a ban in place since last year, over actions they took to "internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian conflict," including pursuing cases against Israel at international tribunals. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas was denied a visa as part of the US move, a Palestinian official said.

item.title: Ultragenyx sets $3.95 million price for rare disease gene therapy
item.description: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical said on Thursday it has set a U.S. list price of $3.95 million for its newly approved gene therapy Fayuvi, launching one of the world's most expensive drugs as a one-time treatment for a rare, fatal childhood disease.
item.dc:creator: Sriparna Roy, Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (RARE.O) said on Thursday it has set a U.S. list price of $3.95 million for its newly approved gene therapy Fayuvi, launching one of the world's most expensive drugs as a one-time treatment for a rare, fatal childhood disease. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Fayuvi for pediatric patients with Sanfilippo syndrome Type A, an inherited condition that progressively damages the brain and nervous system. The disease is caused by a deficiency of an enzyme called sulfamidase, leading to an abnormal accumulation of a complex sugar molecule known as heparan sulfate in the body and brain. This toxic buildup causes children to gradually lose cognitive, speech, and motor skills. Ultragenyx executives said on a conference call that the lifetime cost of caring for a child with the disease, who can spend years in a bedridden state, can exceed $8 million, a burden they said grows as the disease advances. J.P. Morgan analysts estimate Fayuvi could reach peak worldwide sales of $200 million to $250 million. Ultragenyx shares closed 12.6% higher on Thursday. Administered as a single intravenous infusion, the gene therapy delivers a functional copy of the SGSH gene into cells, enabling the body to produce sulfamidase and clear the damaging buildup. In trials, children treated with the therapy maintained or improved cognitive function compared with untreated patients, according to the FDA. Glenn O'Neill, president and co-founder of nonprofit Cure Sanfilippo Foundation, whose daughter Eliza was diagnosed in 2013, and treated with the therapy in 2016 at age 6, said the approval means "real hope and a real life-changing chance to have a different outcome than the traditional course of this disease." Eliza's parents told Reuters ahead of the decision that she has "never had a seizure" and is not on a feeding tube or in a wheelchair, and attends school and swims, outcomes they said far exceed what is typical for the disease. Ultragenyx expects Fayuvi to be available at specialized U.S. treatment centers within 30 to 60 days.

item.title: Amway, affiliates to pay $225 million to settle US claims they deceived recruits
item.description: Multilevel marketing company Amway Corp and two of its affiliates will pay the Federal Trade Commission and Washington State $225 million to resolve allegations it recruited new members with deceptive claims about how much money they could make, the agency said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Multilevel marketing company Amway Corp and two of its affiliates will pay the Federal Trade Commission and Washington State $225 million to resolve allegations it recruited new members with deceptive claims about how much money they could make, the agency said on Thursday. Amway and affiliates World Wide Group LLC and Leadership Team Development Inc told potential recruits that they could make $40,000 or more, according to the FTC. But most of those who joined the two affiliates after 2020 ended up spending more money on training and Amway products than they made, after they were encouraged to buy products that they did not want in order to earn compensation from Amway, the FTC said. "We fundamentally disagree with the agencies’ characterization of our business," an Amway spokesperson said, adding that Amway members are required to follow robust standards of conduct as part of their contract. The $225 million will largely go to repay Amway members affected by the conduct, the FTC said. Amway also agreed to change its practices to disincentivize members from making their primary activity being buying products themselves and recruiting others to do so, the FTC said. The FTC said the settlement is the largest in an FTC action against a multilevel marketing company.

item.title: Prince Harry makes first public appearances 'back on British soil'
item.description: Britain's Prince Harry made his first public appearance on Thursday since he and his wife Meghan returned to Britain after six years in California, saying, "It's good to be back on British soil."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Prince Harry made his first public appearance on Thursday since he and his wife Meghan [USN:L8N44N0XA TEXT:"returned to Britain"] after six years in California, saying, "It's good to be back on British soil." Harry, the younger son of King Charles, relocated last month with Meghan and their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, surprising even their close family. The royal attended the inaugural Invictus Spirit Awards in London, which are linked to the Invictus Games, the sporting competition for wounded, injured and sick military veterans that he founded. Earlier, Harry spoke at an event focused on improving the care of children wounded in conflict hosted by charity Save the Children and Imperial College London. His appearances came on a [USN:L8N4590QP TEXT:"busy day for Britain's royals"], with Charles hosting a [USN:L1N4590CK TEXT:"conference for AI leaders"] amid [USN:L8N4581JE TEXT:"criticism"] in a forthcoming book by the brother of his late first wife, Diana. The book by Charles Spencer is being serialised in the Daily Mail. In the latest extracts published on Thursday, [USN:L8N4591RV TEXT:"Spencer said"] King Charles sounded "like a lottery winner" after the death of Diana.

item.title: Trump says progress made toward establishing US Army base in Poland
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland, crediting "the bold leadership" of Polish President Karol Nawrocki.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland, crediting "the bold leadership" of Polish President Karol Nawrocki. "If this happens, the location will be announced very soon. This will be a historic step for our Great U.S./Polish Alliance," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. Nawrocki later thanked Trump on X, saying that Poland was "ready to continue our efforts to strengthen our defense cooperation," and adding: "I can assure you that the Polish government will do its utmost to provide the best possible location for the US Army base." The head of the Polish president's chancellery, Zbigniew Bogucki, called it "great news for Poland," underscoring that it came on the 87th anniversary of Soviet Russia's invasion of Poland. Poland has been pushing for a bigger allied presence on NATO's eastern flank after Russia's invasion of neighboring Ukraine in 2022. In June, Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz [USN:L8N42Q124 TEXT:"said"] the US Department of Defense was open to Poland's offer to host a permanent US military presence in Poland, but that no decision had been taken. The minister met with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in June in Brussels, where the Pentagon chief announced a new review of US troop deployments in Europe. Poland has so far hosted US troops on a rotational basis.

item.title: Trump dice que se han logrado avances para establecer una base del Ejército de EEUU en Polonia
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el jueves que se están logrando progresos para establecer una base del Ejército de Estados Unidos en Polonia, y atribuyó el mérito al "audaz liderazgo" del mandatario polaco Karol Nawrocki.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el jueves que se están logrando progresos para establecer una base del Ejército de Estados Unidos en Polonia, y atribuyó el mérito al "audaz liderazgo" del mandatario polaco Karol Nawrocki. "Si esto se hace realidad, la ubicación se anunciará muy pronto. Será un paso histórico para nuestra gran alianza entre EEUU y Polonia", dijo Trump en una publicación en Truth Social. Más tarde, Nawrocki agradeció a Trump a través de X, afirmando que Polonia estaba "lista para continuar nuestros esfuerzos por fortalecer la cooperación en materia de defensa". Agregó que "puedo asegurarles que el gobierno polaco hará todo lo posible para ofrecer la mejor ubicación posible para la base del Ejército de Estados Unidos". El jefe de la cancillería presidencial polaca, Zbigniew Bogucki, calificó la noticia de "magnífica para Polonia", subrayando que se producía en el 87.º aniversario de la invasión de Polonia por parte de la Rusia soviética. Polonia ha estado presionando para lograr una mayor presencia aliada en el flanco oriental de la OTAN tras la invasión rusa de la vecina Ucrania en 2022. En junio, el ministro de Defensa polaco, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, dijo que el Departamento de Defensa de Estados Unidos se mostraba receptivo a la oferta de Polonia de albergar una presencia militar estadounidense permanente en el país, aunque señaló que aún no se había tomado ninguna decisión. El ministro se reunió en junio en Bruselas con el secretario de Defensa de Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, ocasión en la que el jefe del Pentágono anunció una nueva revisión del despliegue de tropas estadounidenses en Europa. Hasta la fecha, Polonia ha acogido tropas estadounidenses bajo un régimen de rotación.

item.title: 'I'm Russian,' Ovechkin says about decision to appear in ad for Putin-backed United Russia
item.description: Alexander Ovechkin said on Thursday that he agreed to appear in a political campaign advertisement for the United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, because he supports his country.
item.dc:creator: Brad Ulery
item.content:encoded: Alexander Ovechkin said on Thursday that he agreed to appear in a political campaign advertisement for the United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, because he supports his country. "I'm Russian, and I support my country," Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time leading goalscorer, told reporters at the Washington Capitals' media day. "I'm for peace and love, and I hope in the world it doesn't matter who you are, I hope everybody understands, everybody wants peace and everybody hope everything is going to be okay in the world." Russia will hold a parliamentary election from September 18 to 20, the first since it launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Ovechkin, who can be seen standing behind Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in the video, said he was asked to participate and did not hesitate to agree. He added that he will live in Russia following the end of his career. "As soon as I'm done playing hockey, I'm probably going to stay there," he said. "I'm gonna live there, my kids gonna live there, family. I'm for peace and love and I hope everything's going to be okay." Ovechkin has faced scrutiny over his longstanding ties to Putin as Russia wages war in Ukraine. In 2017 he formed a [USN:KBN1D22LC TEXT:"public movement"] in support of Putin and his Instagram profile picture is a photo of him and the Russian president. He [USN:L1N2V03AT TEXT:"called for peace"] in February 2022 following his home country's invasion of Ukraine. When asked about his support for Putin at the time, he said, "Well, he is my president. But ... I am not in politics. I am an athlete and ... I hope everything is going to be done soon." Ovechkin, who turned 41 on Thursday, has scored 929 goals in 1,573 regular-season NHL games and the upcoming season will be his 22nd in the league. He led the Capitals to a Stanley Cup in 2018.

item.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest since January 2025, Freddie Mac says
item.description: The interest rate on the most common U.S. home loan rose to a 20-month high this week, mortgage giant Freddie Mac said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The interest rate on the most common U.S. home loan rose to a 20-month high this week, mortgage giant Freddie Mac said on Thursday. The rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 6.95% as of Wednesday - the highest since January 2025 - from 6.76% last week, Freddie Mac said.

item.title: Latam markets inch higher in global risk-on mood after Fed hike
item.description: Most Latin American stocks and currencies rose on Thursday, lifted by a global risk-on mood as Treasury yields and the dollar eased after the Federal Reserve's latest rate hike reinforced its resolve to contain inflation.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: Most Latin American stocks and currencies rose on Thursday, lifted by a global risk-on mood as Treasury yields and the dollar eased after the Federal Reserve's latest rate hike reinforced its resolve to contain inflation. MSCI's index tracking regional stocks (.MILA00000PUS) edged higher by 0.6%. With Brazil's presidential elections fast approaching, market focus remained pinned on the contest. An [USN:S8N44200N TEXT:"AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll"] showed Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva remain statistically tied in a simulated runoff ahead of next month's vote. Surveys lately continue to point towards a neck-and-neck race, with market sentiment influenced by shifts in the electoral odds. Against this backdrop, President Lula [USN:L1N4590JP TEXT:"announced a 15% increase"] in cash transfers under the country's flagship welfare program, Bolsa Familia, to shore up his support ahead of the election. The program could add to investor anxiety over the deteriorating public finances under the current government. "Of course, investors associate Bolsonaro with a more fiscally prudent and market-friendly policy agenda," Luca Bindelli, head of investment strategy at Lombard Odier, said. "I don't think Lula's potential win would be outright negative, but it would likely not lead to gains as strong as those under a Bolsonaro victory." On the monetary policy front, Brazil's central bank on Wednesday [USN:L6N458186 TEXT:"cut interest rates by 25 basis points"] for a fifth straight meeting amid firmer signs of an economic slowdown while keeping its options open ahead of the election. "After a series of weaker economic growth data, we think this should help soothe sentiment," Bindelli said. The benchmark Ibovespa index (.BVSP) added 0.5%, while the real inched 0.3% higher. Across the broader currency space, MSCI's index of Latin American currencies (.MILA00000CUS) dipped 0.06%. The U.S. dollar was down 0.05% after touching seven-week highs, while U.S. Treasury yields fell as investors digested the Federal Reserve's widely anticipated rate hike and policymakers' signals of further tightening. Analysts said markets took comfort from the removal of immediate uncertainty around the Fed's decision, despite its hawkish tone. The global inflation outlook remained uncertain this year, mainly due to the ongoing Middle East conflict. Potential trade-related disruptions and persistently high energy prices are keeping central banks cautious. Elsewhere in the region, Politica reported that US President Donald Trump and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum spoke by phone on Wednesday as the [USN:FWN4590VF TEXT:"two countries close in on a trade agreement"]. The Mexican peso gained 0.4%, after hitting an over-one-month low of 17.2710 a dollar in the prior session. Mexico's benchmark stock index (.MXX) rose 0.5%, as trading resumed following a holiday on Wednesday. [USN:L1N4590VL TEXT:"Argentina's economy grew 2.0%"] in the second quarter from a year earlier, beating analyst expectations as mining, agriculture and exports helped support economic activity. The unemployment rate [USN:S0N3VJ05D TEXT:"reached 7.9% in the second quarter"] of 2026, rising from the 7.6% registered in the same period a year earlier. Argentina's stock index (.MERV) gained 1.2%, while the country's currency was up 0.3%.
